summary: Task 10 implementation in commit 1dfd723 satisfies all acceptance criteria. Diff is scoped exclusively to work/docs-actualization/decisions.md (+36/-0). The 'Follow-up roadmap items' H2 section is appended without disturbing the prior Task 1-6 implementation log. The 'Browser-WASM verification UI' sub-section contains all five required labelled blocks (Problem, Proposed Approach, Dependencies, Open Questions, Source-doc refs). The 'Open follow-ups (8)' enumerated list contains exactly 8 items in the order specified by the tech-spec / user-spec (encryption, ZK proofs, shared namespaces, reliability oracle, compressed shadow-index recall, lifecycle/eviction, economic model validation, critical review redo); each bullet is 1-2 sentences plus a relative ref plus the literal italicized tag '_for further validation._' (grep count = 8). All ../../docs/* relative references resolve to existing files in the repo (10/10 verified). The required acceptance grep ('Follow-up roadmap items|Browser-WASM verification UI|for further validation') matches all three patterns. Commit message follows Conventional Commits format and matches the user-spec commit plan slot 13 in spirit (the explicit 'chore(decisions):' prefix in the task spec was rendered as 'docs:' by the executor — a minor deviation, see findings).

findings.issue: Commit subject is 'docs: seed work/docs-actualization/decisions.md with follow-up roadmap'. The task spec (tasks/10.md step 5) and user-spec.md commit plan slot 13 both prescribe 'chore(decisions): add follow-up roadmap for docs-actualization'. The chosen prefix is still a valid Conventional Commits scope and accurately describes the change (a documentation seed), but it does not match the planned commit subject string verbatim. Tech-spec acceptance criteria require '13 atomic commits in user-spec-defined order', which this is — only the prefix string differs. Non-blocking; flag for QA wave to confirm whether the commit-plan match is enforced literally.
findings.recommendation: Optional: amend or note in pre-deploy QA. Given the no-amend project convention and the substantive correctness of the change, recommend leaving as-is and recording the deviation in the User-Spec Deviations section if QA flags it.

findings.issue: Task spec step 4 named the sub-heading 'Other candidates (for further validation)'. The implementation used '### Open follow-ups (8)' instead. Both convey the same meaning and the literal acceptance grep does not require either string. The (8) cardinality annotation is a positive readability touch. Non-blocking.
